cards.title: Early Civilzations in Mesoamerica
body: The Americas stretch from the Arctic Ocean in the north to Cape Horn at the tip of South America, it consists North America, Meso-America and South America. Its inhabitants came from Asia to North America through the Bering Strait during the Ice Age (100,000-8,000 B.C.E) and expanded into the Americas in around 10,000 B.C.E.
The 2 major civilizations of Mesoamerica were the Mayan and Aztec.

cards.title: 1) Mayan Civilization (300-900 C.E)
body: Politics- Flourished on the Yucatan Peninsula and included much of Central and Southern America, it was composed of city-states governed by divine hereditary ruling class. They used Pyramids as tombs of the upper class.

Society- the included the upper class ( Nobles, scribes and preists), middle class (artisans, officials and merchants) and peasants. There was a division of labor; men hunted while women did the domestic work.
Economy- agriculture was the main activity followed by trade through barter. Their cities had public buildings, temples, palaces and pyramids.
Religion- they were polytheistic, their gods were associated with serpents, the Sun, moon and fire. They practiced Human sacrifice in ceremonies and to please the gods.
Writing System- used a sophisticated system based on hieroglyphs (pictures) written on bark, clay, bone and stone, to record the lives of rulers, religious and astronomical information.

Calendar- their 2 types of calendar were based on the belief in the cycles of life; creation and destruction. They believed the world was created in 3113 B.C and was going to vanish in December 23 of 2012. The Solar calendar, closest to the Julian Calendar, had 365 days divided into 18 months of 20 days and extra 5 days. The Sacred Calendar had 260 days divided into 13 weeks of 2o days and was used for religious purposes.
Decline (790-889 C.E)- 1) Natural Disasters
2) Peasant revolts
3) Internal warfare
4) Foreign invasions

cards.title: 2) Aztec Civilization
body: The Aztecs moved from Western Mexico and set up their capital at Tenochtitlan (Lake Texcoco, modern Mexico City) after being pushed by other people in 1325. They began to build their cities and expanded over Mexico.

Politics-the empire was a collection of semi-independent territories under local lords. The King was believed to have a divine rule and was assisted by a council of lords who were given land for their services.

Society- was composed of the upper class, commoners, indentured workers (contracted workers in a lord’s estate) and slaves. Boys were raised to be warriors while girls in domestic works or to become priestesses.

Religion- they were polytheistic, their chief god was Huitzilopochtli (god of sun and war). They believed in the struggle between good and evil which had led to the creation and destruction of 4 suns and the fifth is destined to end by an earthquake. To delay this destruction, they practiced Human sacrifice. They used pyramids as shrines.
Economy- Irrigation farming was their main source of income, they built terraces, fertilizers and the Chinampas (floating gardens) they also had trade and manufacture.
Writing System and Calendar- they used a crude form of writing. The Aztecs had 2 types of calendars; with 260 and 365 days.
Decline- 1. Internal crisis

2. Spanish invasion- led by Hernan Cortes allied with Aztec city- states and was welcomed by King Montezuma as gods in 1519. The people started to rebel in 1520 and were killed by the Spaniards and by an epidemic (Small Pox).

cards.title: Inca Civilization
body: Grew from a small community in Cuzco (southern Peru) into an Empire under the leadership of Pachacuti in 1440’s.

Politics- Pachacuti’s successors expanded the Empire through war into Ecuador, central Chile and the edge of the Amazon basin; it had a population of 12 million people. It had the largest army of 200,000 troops and all Incans were obliged to render unpaid labor service in building projects such as the 40,000 kms long roads. The Empire was divided into 4 quarters ruled by governors, and each quarter into provinces.
Economy- depended on irrigated agriculture, they produced 20 types of corn and 240 types of potatoes. The land was very rich in gold and silver and this attracted the Spaniards.

Culture and Science- they had extensive knowledge in architecture, medicine, calendar, theatre, poetry and plays. They had no writing system but used the Quipu (knotted strings), but most of their art and architecture was destroyed by the Spaniards and most of the gold was taken to Spain.

cards.title: Decline
body: 1. Spanish invasion led by Francisco Pizzarro introduced the small pox killing many people after the Incas welcomed them as gods. Pizzarro created a Spanish Empire with its center at Lima.
2. Epidemic- Small Pox
3. Civil war between the 2 sons the Emperor after he died of small pox, Atahuallpa won over his brother but was killed by the Spaniards
